title: The shop rejected PayPal's signed messages

step.title: PayPal sent each refund 3 times; the shop answered 401 on all three tries.

cause.explanation: A changed line parses or rewrites the request body before the signature is checked, so the bytes that are verified are not the bytes PayPal signed.

replay.expectation: The good build answers 200 and books the events; the bad build answers 401 and books nothing.

fix.claim: Behaves like the good build and PayPal's answer on these 15 inputs (3 orders x arrival order, reversed, tampered).

checks.label: The edits name changed lines of the diff, and replace or delete only lines the cause cited.
It uses only the imports and names a handler may use.
Lines of the bad deploy that the cause did not cite are unchanged, byte for byte.
The edits stay inside the bad deploy's changed hunks.

controls.label: The events in the order they arrived: same answers and same books as the good build.
The same events, last one first: same answers and same books as the good build.
One amount in each body changed: 401 and nothing booked, like the good build.
The books equal PayPal's own answer for the order (GET capture).

certificate.footnote: Orders that were approved but never captured cannot be counted (PayPal has no list API for them). An event that is not in PayPal's event list cannot be shown to have existed. Transaction Search lags about 97-128 minutes, so the last 2 hours of transactions were not used. This certificate is not signed: anyone could edit it.
ownerView: We checked 3 of your 3 orders against PayPal's own records.
